rules.statement: The cause of action for a penal action accrues to the plaintiff when he files papers in the District Court and asks for leave to sue, not when he first discovers the wrongdoing.
rules.supporting_quote: "I find that in the very case Forbes v. Samuel (supra) Scrutton J. paraphrases the sentence, in an earlier case,-'on filing an information the informer has a right to the penalty vested in him'-to mean that on filing the information the informer 'secures his position against a later informant'. Even if one interprets the principle in those English cases—that the party first coming to Court 'attaches' the right of action to himself—to mean that the cause of action accrues only when the party comes to Court, then the cause of action in this case accrued to the plaintiff in July, 1936, when he filed papers in the District Court and asked for leave to sue the respondent."
